title: Operator-Composition Variance in robomimic Multi-Human Benchmarks: preregistration, code, and results
description:
Preregistered audit of how the uncertainty reported on the robomimic Multi-Human (MH) benchmarks decomposes into training seed, demonstration resampling, operator composition, and rollout noise.

Contents: the preregistration with three dated amendments; the pinned environment and dataset checksums; immutable partition files; fixed evaluation initial conditions; the training and evaluation queues; per-run and per-rollout results for 138 BC-RNN runs (6,900 rollouts) and a 500-rollout re-evaluation of 46 Square checkpoints (23,000 rollouts); and the scripts that regenerate every number, table and figure in the accompanying paper.

Outcome: the preregistered claim that operator-composition variance exceeds seed variance was not supported on any task. The data show that the conventional three-seed, 50-rollout statistic is dominated by rollout noise on Lift and Can and cannot resolve differences below about 13 points on Square.
